The current study has found promising results in biomolecular identification of allergenic pollen through real-time PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) analysis. This approach, when combined with the use of multiplex real-time PCR, allows for the simultaneous detection of different taxa within a single reaction tube, providing more comprehensive data on pollen composition and diversity.

This new perspective has significant implications for aerobiological monitoring, enabling researchers to better understand the complex relationships between pollen types, environmental factors, and human health. The ability to rapidly identify specific pollen allergens can lead to improved diagnosis and treatment of allergic reactions, such as hay fever and respiratory issues.

Furthermore, this technology can be applied in various settings, including laboratories, fieldwork, and even clinical practice, offering a valuable tool for monitoring air quality and predicting allergy-related events. By expanding our understanding of pollen composition and its relationship with human health, we may uncover new avenues for developing innovative treatments and prevention strategies for allergies.

The findings of this study highlight the importance of biomolecular identification in aerobiological monitoring, emphasizing the need for continued research and development to improve our ability to detect and analyze pollen allergens.
